title: The Pile at the Edge
hook: Somebody left a ridge of gravel along the shoulder.
scene: A windrow runs the right edge for the next half mile — loose gravel piled where the grader pushed it and never came back. It looks like shoulder. It is a rope laid along the road.

source.psdp_skill: Skill twelve: driving on rural roads
source.teaching_target: PSDP twelve — gravel windrow / pile at the edge. PSDP-only (n/a DOL).

image_brief.subject: SUBJECT through FULL-GRID mesh: a continuous low GRAVEL WINDROW — a plowed/grader-pushed berm of loose gravel and debris along the RIGHT shoulder edge, like a rope for the next half mile; travel track CLEAR LEFT of the berm; NOT a cut slope, embankment wall, quarry face, or steep bank; locked cabin carrier INBOARD on passenger floor: hard-sided; wire grille door facing inboard; Gracie's orange tabby markings visible behind the grille; belt routed through the handle
image_brief.foreground: worn black wheel LEFT (match VI-001-6 / VI-002-8 cabin geometry); faded pink dash DARK/UNLIT — no lit green turn arrows; ANALOG gauges with VISIBLE needles and dial faces (odo/trip OK; NOT blank/black empty circles); no speedlike 112 LCD; FULL-GRID welded steel mesh over the entire windshield (VI-009 cage canon) — not a low dash-level band; missing windshield cage is a hard FAIL; Gracie carrier ONLY INSIDE the cabin on the passenger floor / seat (INBOARD) — hard-sided; wire grille door facing inboard toward driver; Gracie's orange tabby markings visible behind the grille; belt routed through the handle; carrier is BEHIND the mesh plane, in the cabin volume with the wheel — NEVER on the hood, NEVER outside the windshield, NEVER mounted on the exterior of the cage
image_brief.midground: proper windrow: continuous low ridge of loose gravel piled along the RIGHT edge (grader berm / debris berm) running away like a rope; clear graded travel track LEFT of the windrow where the tires belong; fir crowding the ditch beyond the berm; windrow height roughly tire-sidewall / low berm — NOT a cut slope or tall embankment
image_brief.background: Cascades-west PNW wet backcountry — restricted sightlines, second-growth fir crowding the shoulder, blackberry and alder in the ditch, vegetation close to the road, wet gray asphalt or graded gravel; NOT sage, dry grass, bare hills, or long open highway; soft wet dirt beyond the pile; no other cars
image_brief.read: loose gravel is piled in a continuous windrow berm along the right edge for a long stretch; travel track clear left of it; locked carrier INSIDE cabin; dark dash with readable gauges

no cat loose on the seat
no "ginger tabby" wording — use orange tabby markings behind the grille
no carrier door facing outboard toward camera
no empty carrier with no cat visible behind grille
no belt not routed through handle
no low dash-level mesh band only
no brightly lit dash by default
no speedlike 112 LCD readout (odo/trip numerals OK if not live speed)
no desert GPS / arid nav HUD
Ali alone — only VI-013 has a second person
no cut slope as the subject
no embankment wall as the subject
no quarry face / steep bank substituting for windrow
no tall vertical gravel wall beside the road
no carrier mounted on exterior of mesh/cage
no carrier ahead of the glass plane
no empty black gauge circles without needles

decision: The windrow is on your right. Where do you put the tires?

options.text: Left of it, in the graded track, and give it room
options.result: You stay in the part somebody meant you to drive on. The pile sits out there being a pile.

options.text: Straddle it so you are using the full width
options.result: One wheel in loose and one in packed, and the car starts arguing with itself about which way is straight.

options.text: Ride the far right so oncoming traffic has all the room it wants
options.result: You put the right side into the windrow to be generous. It takes the wheel out of your hands and points you at the ditch.
It is gravel that is six inches deep in a line. That is not the same gravel you are already on.

debrief: Watch for windrows — piled gravel at the road edge grabs a wheel.
